learningObjective: Advance one start cursor by batch size and yield the half-open slice; sequence slicing automatically clips the final end.

mechanismReview.pattern: Fixed-stride half-open slicing over a sequence.
mechanismReview.recognitionCue: Use it when every item must appear once in consecutive batches and the final batch may be shorter than the requested size.
mechanismReview.invariant: Before each yield, indexes below start have appeared exactly once; items[start:start+batch_size] contributes the next non-overlapping range, clipped only by sequence length.
mechanismReview.stateModel: Retain the immutable items, positive batch_size, and current start generated by range; Python slicing supplies the effective end.
mechanismReview.visualRationale: The full indexed input remains visible while stable start and included-end markers move by one batch, with half-open bounds and clipping arithmetic printed in every frame.
rejectedAlternatives: Reshaping requires divisibility or padding and does not match the final-short-batch contract.
Dropping the last short slice loses valid examples.
Showing only three output lists hides stride, half-open boundaries, and the positive-size guard.
mechanismReview.transferLesson: Use half-open slices and a fixed stride to partition ordered data without overlap; let bounded slicing handle a short tail explicitly.

mediumRationale: An original, problem-specific trace shows the actual input, changing state, safe transition, and result. The static first frame works without JavaScript; controls add step-by-step playback without replacing the proof with decoration.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic graph layout would hide the exact data values and state changes that this problem needs.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: the trace is a changing data state, so semantic HTML keeps values selectable, readable, and responsive.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: each problem owns concrete frames rendered as arrays, maps, grids, trees, stacks, queues, intervals, pointers, bits, or tensor shapes.
mediumComparison.interaction: Selected as progressive enhancement: Play, Previous, Next, and step buttons reveal the same authored frames while static HTML remains complete.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the visual is an original synthesis of the supplied implementation and does not reuse source artwork.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose alone would make the learner simulate the changing data structure in working memory.
